newsitem.title: USA: EDS posts higher quarter net amid spin-off charge.
newsitem.headline: EDS posts higher quarter net amid spin-off charge.

text.p: Electronic Data Systems Corp., spun off last year from General Motors Corp., Thursday reported higher fourth quarter earnings.
Excluding an $850 million charge and $45.5 million in costs related to the spin-off last June from its former parent, EDS also reported higher results for the year.
"Worldwide, the information technology services and management consulting industries are very robust, and there is strong growth in the markets that we serve," said EDS Chairman Les Alberthal.

The global information services company said fourth quarter net income rose 1.2 percent, to $272.8 million in 1996 from $269.5 million a year earlier. Earnings per share were flat at 56 cents a share, slightly below the expectations of industry analysts.
Quarterly revenues rose to $4 billion from $3.6 billion. EDS said it signed $3.07 billion in new contracts in the fourth quarter, bringing the total for the year to $8.4 billion.
Even with the fourth quarter increase in new contracts, last year's total of $8.4 billion was still below the levels recorded in the previous two years.

For the year, net income rose nearly 7 percent, to $1 billion, or $2.07 a share, from $938.9 million, or $1.96 a share, in 1995 before a one-time $850 million charge the company took in the second quarter and $45.5 million in costs related to EDS' split-off last June from GM.
EDS stock rose 62.5 cents to close at $46.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Plano, Texas-based company's stock price has fallen sharply in recent months amid concerns that it was getting insufficient new business to make up for a decline in sales to GM.
